saturation.interpretation: The deterministic policy simulator does not saturate the top of the score scale.

checks.threshold: sovereign_hybrid average must exceed centralized_cloud by at least 20 points
checks.interpretation: The scorecard should punish raw convenience-first disclosure enough that it cannot look competitive.

checks.threshold: brokered_tool_agent average must exceed centralized_cloud by at least 20 points
checks.interpretation: A consent-mediated tool path should remain clearly better than raw centralized disclosure.

checks.threshold: centralized_cloud privacy average must be 45 or lower
checks.interpretation: The privacy metric should not give near-passing marks to a raw external-disclosure baseline.

checks.threshold: centralized_cloud user-control average must be 45 or lower
checks.interpretation: The user-control metric should punish unconsented boundary crossing.

checks.threshold: sovereign_hybrid average must exceed local_only by at least 3 points
checks.interpretation: The scorecard should not reward blanket refusal as equivalent to consented usefulness.

checks.threshold: no more than 10% of deterministic policy runs should score 95+
checks.interpretation: If too many synthetic runs saturate the ceiling, the benchmark cannot distinguish excellent systems.

limitations: This is a meta-evaluation over author-defined baselines, not independent measurement validation.
Passing these checks does not prove the scorecard matches human judgment.
The stress report is useful for catching obvious scorecard collapse before external review.
